artworks.title: Jupiter and Io
artworks.description: Correggio's Vienna canvas shows Zeus as a dark cloud embracing Io — the Argive maiden's seduction before the cow-transformation that Hera will force. Oil on canvas, Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

artworks.title: Mercury and Argus
artworks.description: Rubens stages Hermes lulling hundred-eyed Argus while Io, still a heifer, waits for rescue — Hera's watch broken so the wanderer can flee. Oil on canvas, Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

artworks.title: Mercury and Argus
artworks.description: Velázquez darkens the killing of Argus: Mercury with panpipes beside the sleeping guard, Io's bovine form the reason for the murder. Oil on canvas, Museo del Prado, Madrid.

artworks.title: The Myth of Io
artworks.description: A Florentine cassone panel unrolls Io's story in frieze: Zeus' pursuit, the cow, Argus, and Hermes — the Argive wanderer's myth as Renaissance narrative sequence. Tempera on panel, Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

artworks.title: Io watched by Argus (Pompeii fresco)
artworks.description: A Pompeian wall painting from the House of Meleager shows Io with bovine horns under Argus' gaze — the jealous watch before Hermes' rescue, preserved in Naples. Fresco, Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Naples.

popCulture.title: Io (moon)
popCulture.description: Jupiter's volcanic innermost moon keeps the wanderer's name — Io as a world of fire beside the god who pursued her.

popCulture.title: Io (mythology)
popCulture.description: Io remains the cow-maiden driven across continents — Hera's gadfly, the Argive ancestress, and the emblem of divine jealousy.
